findings.reason: as written the section's own control cannot falsify the guard it adds, so a node could deliver the probe half exactly as the plan states and still ship a probe assertion that is unreachable under the control; the plan needs to require the probe assertion be independently observable (its own test, or its own control), not inherit a control already consumed by a sibling assertion.
findings.text: §17's done-when claims "the negative control removes the node-tmp seal from `fence_argv`, and the probe assertion then fails", but the probe assertion it means is the repaired one at `tests/test_a_worker_cannot_remove_the_nodes_temporary_files.py:309`, and the declared control (`declared_seal_mutation`, `:272-278`) strips the seal inside the one test that already carries the pre-existing assertion `assert node.outside.exists()` at `:308`; that assertion fails first under the control, so execution never reaches `:309` and the new probe assertion is never shown to fail — the same assertion the review follow-on ("drop or repair the trivially-true assertion at …:309") was raised to make load-bearing

findings.reason: the invariant is real and true (`fence_argv` composes the same argv, `reckon/_worker_fence.py:1445-1459`), and a worker can execute it by asserting the composed argv against a literal captured at base, so the loose phrasing costs an interpretation, not a wrong mechanism.
findings.text: §17's done-when also asks for "a test [that] finds that the composed fence argv for a fixed set of roots is identical before and after the change", but a test in the delivered tree has no "before" to compare against, so the clause as phrased names no runnable arm
